title: How to Manage Contracts for Outsourced Maintenance
summary: See how to manage contracts with outsourced maintenance vendors, with version control and connected records.
body_markdown:
Managing outsourced maintenance contracts means each vendor agreement stays versioned and connected to the properties they service, with renewal dates flagged automatically instead of tracked in a separate spreadsheet. In **Jestor** , this uses the same version-controlled contract structure applied to any vendor relationship.


Outsourced maintenance relationships often span several vendors across a portfolio, each with their own contract terms and renewal dates — exactly the kind of tracking that degrades quickly without structure.


## What unstructured maintenance contract tracking misses


- Multiple vendor contracts with no consolidated view of terms and renewal dates
- No connection between a maintenance contract and the properties it actually covers
- Manual monitoring of renewal dates, easy to let slip
- No clear history of contract changes or renegotiated terms over time


## How structured contract management works


- Maintenance vendor contracts stay versioned, connected to the properties they cover
- Automations flag contracts approaching renewal or expiration
- Version history preserves prior terms alongside the current agreement
- Contracts connect to the same vendor record used for work order tracking


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Version history removes ambiguity about which contract terms are current
- Contracts stay connected to both the vendor and the specific properties covered
- Automated renewal flags reduce reliance on manual monitoring
- The same vendor record ties contracts to actual work performed

## Frequently Asked Questions


**Can a maintenance contract cover multiple properties?** Yes, through relational connections to each covered property. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Are renewal reminders automated?** Yes, through automations tied to the contract's dates.


**Does this replace legal review of maintenance agreements?** No, it structures tracking; legal review still applies as needed.
